title: Hazards and Risks — Physical, Chemical, Biological and Management of Hazards
shortDescription: Hazard types, risk analysis and the control measures that bring risk down.
genZNote: Hazard = what can hurt you. Risk = how likely and how bad. Examiners love testing whether you know the difference.

sections.heading: Types of Hazards
sections.body: Allergens commonly declared: cereals containing gluten, crustaceans, eggs, fish, peanuts, soybeans, milk, tree nuts and sulphites (≥10 mg/kg).

table.caption: Hazard classes
rows: Heat treatment, temperature control, hygiene, acidification
Pesticide/vet-drug residues, heavy metals (Pb, Hg, Cd, As), additives overuse, allergens, cleaning-chemical residues, acrylamide, 3-MCPD
Supplier approval, MRLs, allergen control, correct chemical storage
Glass, metal, stone, wood, bone, plastic, hair
Sieves, magnets, metal detectors, X-ray, GMP, glass policy

sections.heading: Risk Analysis
bullets: Codex risk analysis has three parts: risk assessment (hazard identification, hazard characterisation, exposure assessment, risk characterisation), risk management and risk communication.
Risk = likelihood × severity; use risk matrices to prioritise.
Reference values: ADI (acceptable daily intake), TDI, MRL (maximum residue limit), ALARA principle for contaminants.

sections.heading: Management of Hazards
bullets: Prevention first: PRPs, supplier verification, specifications, hygienic design.
Control: critical control points with critical limits, monitoring and corrective action (HACCP).
Verification and validation: testing, audits, calibration, review.
Contingency: traceability, withdrawal and recall plans, crisis management.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Hazards are biological, chemical or physical agents with potential to harm; risk analysis and layered controls manage them to acceptable levels.
keyFacts: Three hazard classes: biological, chemical, physical.
ADI and MRL are safety reference values.

highYieldFacts: Allergens are chemical (protein) hazards for sensitive individuals.
commonTraps: Do not say hazard and risk mean the same.

sources.name: Codex General Principles of Food Hygiene (CXC 1-1969)

questions.explanation: The three components are assessment, management, communication.
